title: fix(components): a dependent lookup clears when its dependsOn parent changes or clears (objectui#11631)
body:
Fixes #11631

Clause-②: no

## What changed

A lookup whose field-level `dependsOn` names a sibling field now drops its selection when that sibling changes or is cleared. Before, the picker re-scoped its candidate query to the new parent but kept the record already picked. So the form saved an invoice whose contact belongs to a different account, and the server, which checks only that a reference exists, accepted it.

`@object-ui/components`, `renderers/form/form.tsx`:

- `dependentLookupParents` (module scope, not exported) answers which sibling fields scope a lookup. It reads the same slot `LookupField` scopes its query by: the `field` prop this renderer hands the widget (`field.field || field`), one nested `field` unwrapped when it carries `reference` or `type`, and only the array shape the spec declares at field level. The family is `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES`, the set `needsDataSourceWiring` already feeds `dependentValues` to. `CASCADE_OPTION_WIDGET_TYPES` is untouched.
- A `form.watch` subscription (keyed on the primitive `dependentLookupsKey`, established only when the form has a dependent lookup) clears a lookup when any parent takes a different value. It writes `null`, or `[]` for a multi-value lookup, the same sentinels the two existing clears write, so an edit overwrites the stored value instead of leaving it. A lookup holding nothing is never written to. A cleared lookup that scopes another lookup clears that one in the same pass. The field whose change started a pass is never cleared by it, so two lookups that name each other cannot wipe the pick the user just made.
- What does not count as a parent change: a `defaultValues` reset (a record landing after first paint, a `recordId` swap in a mounted drawer, the input the reset carries across, read inside `resetInFlightRef`), and a notification that names no field (the bare `form.reset()` that `resetOnSubmit` and Cancel call). Those re-base the comparison and clear nothing, so an existing record opens with its saved pair intact.

The `Clause-②` declaration holds: no export, prop, type member or i18n key is added to any `@object-ui/*` package. `resolveDependsOnFields` was already exported by `@object-ui/core` and is only imported here.

## Landing site: `form.tsx`, beside the reset, not inside the cascade-clear effect

The card names the cascade-clear effect. That effect is the right file but the wrong mechanism for a lookup, measured both ways:

- It skips every field whose normalized type is not in `CASCADE_OPTION_WIDGET_TYPES` and every field with no static `options`. A lookup fails both checks (A0 below: all seven clear rows red on the unchanged file).
- It is a passive effect over `ruleRecord`, and it validates a value against an option set. A lookup has no option set to test, so its rule has to be a transition (the parent moved). A passive effect after the commit sees two value sets and no record of which operation moved them. The `defaultValues` reset that fills a parent and its lookup together runs inside the synchronous `resetInFlightRef` window, and only a subscriber notified inside that window can tell it from an edit. That is the same signal the `onAction` / `onChange` value channels in this file already read, so the new subscription sits beside them. The option effect's comment now names it.

## Measured

### Unit pins (`form-dependent-lookup-clear-11631.test.tsx`, 14 rows)

Clear rows: create, parent switched; edit, parent emptied (explicit `null` survives `JSON.stringify`); hand-written field carrying `dependsOn` itself; multi-value lookup to `[]`; two-level chain; two lookups naming each other.
Keep rows: edit with the pair present at mount; record landing after first paint (then a real switch still clears); `recordId` swap; input carried across a defaults reset; `resetOnSubmit`; unrelated field change; empty lookup not written to; a bare-name `dependsOn` the picker does not scope by.

### Reverse verification and ablations (fix committed first; every leg restored from HEAD and proved by blob hash and empty `git diff HEAD`)

Direction predicted before running: the clear rows go red in the STALE direction and the keep rows stay green; each guard ablation reds exactly the row that pins it. Observed exactly that:

| Leg | Mutation | Red rows |
|---|---|---|
| A0 | `form.tsx` at the pre-fix base | 7: the six clear rows plus the after-paint row's live-afterwards half, every failure a retained value (`prospect-18`, `b1` or the two-id list) where an empty value was expected |
| A1 | subscription never established | the same 7 |
| A2 | drop the `resetInFlightRef` re-base | 1: carried input |
| A3 | drop the unnamed-notification re-base | 1: `resetOnSubmit` |
| A4 | drop the origin guard | 1: lookups naming each other |
| A5 | drop the empty-lookup skip | 1: empty lookup not written to |
| A6 | accept a non-array `dependsOn` | 1: the bare-name boundary |

Mutations went through `ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit 1 to 0, blob changed); the run sits on the report comment.

### Live, card repro: before and after

Backend: objectstack `main` at `75ddcd1b`, showcase app, built in a private worktree, `--fresh` database on a private port. "Before" is the console from this branch's base `c4c506b`; "after" is the console from this branch. Same backend, same browser script (Chromium, headless).

- Served metadata: `/meta/object/showcase_invoice` serves `contact` with `dependsOn: ["account"]` (field level). The contact candidate query under Northwind is `filter=["account","=",NORTHWIND_ID]`.
- New invoice, Account Northwind, Contact "Prospect 18", switch Account to Contoso, Status Draft, Create:
  - before: the chip stays "Prospect 18"; the create body carries Contoso's id and Prospect 18's id; read back: Contoso beside Prospect 18, whose own `account` is Northwind.
  - after: the chip clears on the switch; the create body carries `"contact": null`; read back: `contact` null.
- Same, but remove the Account chip instead of switching: before shows "Prospect 18" beside "Select Account first"; after shows only "Select Account first".
- Edit an existing Northwind / Prospect 18 invoice, change only Tax Rate, Save (after): the contact shows on open, the update body is `{"tax_rate":5}`, and the read-back keeps the pair.
- Edit the same invoice and switch Account to Contoso: before, the update body is the account alone and the stored contact stays Northwind's; after, the update body carries `"contact": null` and the read-back is null.

## Other form paths: not changed here

Every host that draws a `type: 'form'` schema shares this renderer: `ObjectForm` and its drawer, modal, split, tabbed and wizard variants in `@object-ui/plugin-form`. Two other paths keep the defect, by reading:

- `apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx` (the form-view page, `/forms/:name` and `/f/:slug`) is a second renderer with its own `values` state. It feeds lookups `dependentValues` but never clears one. Not measured live: the only dependent lookup in the examples is `showcase_invoice.contact`, and no form view renders it.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/ActionParamDialog.tsx`: a lookup parameter with `dependsOn` is scoped by the dialog's values, and `updateValue` writes only the changed parameter. Not measured live.

## Acceptance notes

- Keeping a selection the new scope still admits was left out, as the triage grade allows. Answering it needs a server query per switch, and the gain is narrow.
- A view-level `dependsOn` on a lookup (the form-view `FormField.dependsOn` that `@object-ui/plugin-form` copies onto the runtime field's top level) does not scope `LookupField` when object metadata is stashed, so it does not drive this clear either. The clear follows the picker's scope by construction, and the boundary row pins the form side of that.
- Inline single-field edits (the record detail inline editor, the grid's inline row edit) save a changed parent without touching its dependent. That is a different interaction, noted only.
- No toast names the cleared lookup: the chip vanishes next to the control the user just changed, and naming it would need a new i18n key, which this change may not add.

## Gates

On the final head `fea2341` (after the merge of `main`): `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components type-check` (its test project lists the new file), `pnpm --filter @object-ui/components lint` (0 errors, no warning in the added hunks), `pnpm exec vitest run packages/components/src/renderers/form/`, the A0 to A6 legs above, and the root checks `check:new-line-citations`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:shell-escape-residue`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`.

Declared narrowing: the whole-package `pnpm exec vitest run packages/components/` ran green at `a3e25ff`. After it came a types-only commit (the metadata carrier read as a record of unknown values instead of `any`, the probe's props declared) and the merge, whose diff touches only `@object-ui/app-shell` and a changeset. The final head reran the form directory instead. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the full `pnpm test` are CI's.

Changeset: `.changeset/11631-lookup-cascade-clear.md`, `@object-ui/components` patch.
